cases.brief: Adopt a refute-first posture. Read references/audit-convergence.md from the repo. Assume the document is wrong. Find gaps, unstated assumptions, missing enforcement mechanisms, or contradictions between the stated convergence criteria and what can actually be verified deterministically. Evidence must be path:line. Output JSON findings only.

Adopt a refute-first posture. Read references/plugin-boundary.md from the repo. Assume the document is wrong. Find security gate gaps, missing invariants, claims that the code cannot actually enforce, and permission escalation vectors that the boundary rules do not close. Evidence must be path:line. Output JSON findings only.

cases.description: Negative case: agy cannot enforce read-only, so dispatch of this read-only audit profile must be rejected fail-closed by the scheduler at the validate stage (2026-06-10 verified). This case passes when dispatch is rejected with an error containing 'cannot enforce read-only'; an actual agy run completing would be a regression of the fail-closed behavior.
cases.brief: Adopt a refute-first posture. Read plugins/adversarial-audit/paths/adversarial-fanout-convergence.json from the repo. Assume the playbook is wrong. Find steps that lack stop conditions, anti-patterns that are declared but not enforced by the path structure, missing evidence requirements, and convergence criteria that could be gamed or trivially satisfied. Evidence must be path:line. Output JSON findings only.
cases.notes: Expected behavior: dispatch is rejected at the validate stage before any agy process is spawned; the rejection error message contains 'cannot enforce read-only'. Do not work around by escalating sandbox or removing the read-only requirement.
